template.name: germany_ug_university_planning
template.description: Advising interview to plan Adrian’s undergraduate study path in Germany. The goal is to surface options, decision factors, requirements, and a concrete application plan.

sections.label: Student Background and Objectives
sections.description: Capture Adrian’s academic record, language proficiency, career aims, and any fixed constraints that shape feasible study paths.

sections.label: Field of Study and Program Features
sections.description: Record target majors/fields and must-have program characteristics (e.g., English- vs. German-taught, practical focus, dual study, accreditation).

sections.label: University Options and Rationale
sections.description: List specific German universities/programs under consideration with reasons for interest, initial pros/cons, and fit notes.

sections.label: Decision Criteria and Preferences
sections.description: Elicit and prioritize the factors that will drive the choice (e.g., location, costs, rankings, language of instruction, internships, campus culture).

sections.label: Admissions Pathways and Requirements
sections.description: Detail eligibility route and required steps (e.g., Uni-Assist/Hochschulstart, Studienkolleg, APS, TestAS, language tests, documents, deadlines).

sections.label: Budget and Funding Plan
sections.description: Estimate tuition/semester fees and living costs, identify funding sources, and note scholarships or aid to pursue (e.g., DAAD, university grants).

sections.label: Constraints and Risks
sections.description: Flag potential blockers or uncertainties (visa timing, housing availability, recognition of credentials, language gaps) and their impact.

sections.label: Application Timeline and Next Actions
sections.description: Define milestones, target intakes, application tasks, owners, and due dates to execute the chosen plan.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and Context
phases.goal: Build rapport, confirm objectives for the meeting, and get a concise snapshot of Adrian’s background and aims.

phases.label: Goals and Options Discovery
phases.goal: Explore fields of interest and surface a concrete list of universities/programs Adrian is considering.

phases.label: Evaluation and Requirements
phases.goal: Clarify decision criteria, check feasibility, and map admissions requirements, costs, and risks for shortlisted options.

phases.label: Plan and Commit
phases.goal: Select a direction, align on application strategy, and commit to a timeline with clear next actions and owners.

issues.description: Phase goals and pacing overreach the user’s brief (“understand which options he is thinking about, what factors play an important role”). The template devotes 55% to requirements and committing to an application plan (phases evaluation_and_requirements at 0.35 and plan_and_commit at 0.2), pushing into admissions, budget, and timeline beyond discovery/evaluation.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-scope and rebalance phases to prioritize options and decision factors: e.g., 1) Rapport/Context (0.1), 2) Options Discovery (0.45) focusing on field_of_study_and_program_features + university_options_and_rationale, 3) Criteria & Comparative Evaluation (0.35) focusing on decision_criteria_and_preferences (with light feasibility checks), 4) Wrap-up & Next Steps (0.1) capturing immediate research tasks rather than a full application plan. Reduce or fold admissions_pathways_and_requirements, budget_and_funding_plan, and constraints_and_risks into a light feasibility snapshot, and keep detailed planning out of scope.

issues.description: decision_criteria_and_preferences is marked repeated=true, which may fragment a single prioritized criteria set across multiple entries.
issues.suggested_fix: Set repeated=false for decision_criteria_and_preferences and capture a single prioritized list with weights/notes.

issues.description: Explicit inclusion of an "other" section is redundant if the system auto-appends one, and it inflates the section list needlessly.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the explicit other section; rely on the auto-appended catch‑all.

critique.rationale: The proposal is well-structured with clear, concrete sections and valid IDs, and it covers options and decision factors. However, its scope and pacing push heavily into admissions planning and timelines, which exceeds the user’s stated aim of exploring options and key decision factors. Minor polish items include the repeated flag for criteria and the redundant other section.
critique.next_iteration_focus: Re-scope and rebalance phases to center on options and decision criteria, de-emphasizing admissions/budget/timeline into a light feasibility check or deferring them.

template.name: germany_undergrad_options_review
template.description: Discovery interview to understand Adrian’s undergraduate study options in Germany and the decision factors guiding his choice. The outcome is a clarified shortlist, prioritized criteria, light feasibility flags, and immediate research tasks.

sections.label: Student Background and Objectives
sections.description: Capture Adrian’s academic record, language levels, target intake, and long‑term aims that bound feasible study options.

sections.label: Fields of Study and Program Features
sections.description: Record target majors/fields and must‑have program characteristics (e.g., English- vs. German‑taught, applied vs. research focus, dual study, accreditation, class size).

sections.label: University Options and Rationale
sections.description: List specific German universities/programs under consideration with reasons for interest, initial pros/cons, and fit notes.

sections.label: Decision Criteria and Preferences
sections.description: Elicit and prioritize the factors driving the decision; mark must‑haves vs. nice‑to‑haves and assign relative importance/weights.

sections.label: Feasibility Snapshot (Light)
sections.description: For each option, note quick feasibility flags: eligibility route hints (direct/Studienkolleg), needed tests (e.g., TestDaF/IELTS/TestAS), current language readiness, ballpark costs, and any clear showstoppers.

sections.label: Comparative Evaluation and Preference Order
sections.description: Synthesize how shortlisted options score against top criteria and record a tentative ranking with key justifications and trade‑offs.

sections.label: Research Tasks and Next Steps
sections.description: Define focused follow‑ups to inform the decision (e.g., verify admissions route, confirm program details, check housing/costs), with owners and near‑term due dates.

sections.label: Other
sections.description: Anything material that doesn't fit a declared section. Prefer declared sections; use this only when nothing else fits.

phases.label: Rapport and Context
phases.goal: Build rapport, confirm meeting goals, and capture a concise snapshot of Adrian’s background and aims.

phases.label: Options Discovery
phases.goal: Surface fields of interest and assemble a concrete list of universities/programs Adrian is considering.

phases.label: Criteria and Comparative Evaluation
phases.goal: Clarify and prioritize decision criteria, perform a light feasibility check, and compare shortlisted options against the criteria.

phases.label: Wrap‑up and Next Steps
phases.goal: Confirm immediate research tasks, owners, and timing to move the decision forward; recap tentative preference.

issues.description: Potential overlap between fields_of_study_and_program_features and decision_criteria_and_preferences — both can attract items like “English‑taught only,” “class size,” etc., causing double entry or mis-bucketing.
issues.suggested_fix: Constrain fields_of_study_and_program_features to program-specific attributes tied to each intended major/track, and reserve decision_criteria_and_preferences for the cross‑option evaluation framework (must‑haves, weights). Add a note in each description clarifying this boundary.

issues.description: Feasibility_snapshot is strong but could miss common Germany-specific gates (e.g., NC thresholds, uni‑assist usage, APS certificate for certain countries, portfolio/practical requirements for some fields).
issues.suggested_fix: Expand the feasibility_snapshot description with a short parenthetical: “include NC thresholds, uni‑assist status, APS (if applicable), and any portfolio/practical prerequisites.”

critique.rationale: Well-structured template with 7 substantive sections and 4 coherent phases whose time allocations sum to 1.0. It directly supports the user’s goals of surfacing Adrian’s options and the decision factors, with sensible flow from background to options, criteria, comparison, and next steps. Minor clarifications will reduce potential mis-bucketing and strengthen Germany-specific feasibility notes.
